answers.correction: Four corrections. (1) Addazi et al. 2022 do take up the identification, as a possibility. Apart from the §2.2.2.3 passage the reader quotes, the review says (§2.2.2.5) that 'each observed quantum field has a “dual”, which could be associated with dark matter', and (§2.3.4) lists 'their “duals”, associated with dark matter degrees of freedom [408]'. It is also not outside the school, since Minic and Kowalski-Glikman are coauthors. That is the record's 'partial'. (2) Two more outside statements using other meanings of 'dual' were missed. Houlden 2015 (proceedings 'Unified Field Mechanics'; not in the record) proposes dark matter as massive vacuum states in Rowlands' 'dual space to the real space where Standard Model fundamental fermions (and we) reside', states that 'interacts gravitationally'. Huang and Huang 1999 put light dark matter 'in a dual SM or two-fold SM'; this is a phrase collision, already in the record as such. (3) Nishimura's dark sector is closer to a counterpart of visible matter than the answer says. As a conditional, the negative-norm sector, assigned to the isospin spacetime, would hold 'almost all the antiparticles'. It is still not momentum space. (4) Ran's report is not new to the record. answers.question: Q3
answers.correction: As worded, 'No outside paper has dual charges or a dual Standard Model' fails on a phrase collision. Huang and Huang (astro-ph/9909321, 1999; Commun. Theor. Phys. 51, 575, 2009) put dark matter 'in a dual SM or two-fold SM'. Their doubling is unrelated to Born duality; the record labels it a collision. A gauge-invisible copy of Standard Model fermions as dark matter is also published outside the school. Pavšič 2022 (in the record as C1 related) has new leptons and quarks under a second U(1)×SU(2): 'For us it is thus “dark matter”'. That is a copy, not a Born dual. The answer also misrenders Bolognesi's scheme (2.4). Only matter and matter~ are linked across (⟺), and each is linked vertically (↕) to its own gauge/gravity. Gauge/gravity and gauge~/gravity~ 'can influence each other only through the matter field'; there is no gauge/gravity ⟷ gauge~/gravity~ arrow. Nishimura's negative-norm sector would, conditionally, hold 'almost all the antiparticles'.

answers.question: Q4
answers.correction: (1) For Häuser and Dröscher, 'by gravity only' is an inference from abstracts. They say dark matter is 'principally invisible' and 'principally undetectable', and that its gravitational interaction is 'directly perceptible'; neither says 'only'. Part II's abstract also has a quintessence particle that 'mediates an interaction between ordinary matter ... and the ubiquitous scalar field of dark energy'. (2) Chouha's 'entangled' is the duality constraint p·p̃ = μ, 'which couples the geometric and dual momentum sectors' (Ẽ = μ/E). It is a property of one metaparticle, not a correlation between dark and visible matter. (3) Nishimura's universe is a product state: 'the wave function of the universe will generally be the direct product of the positive and negative norm wave functions'. By my reading that is uncorrelated, the opposite of the school's 'correlated'. (4) For Ran, the report itself says 'the absence of outward radiation is guaranteed by the evanescent structure of the state rather than by any ad-hoc restriction on its charge content', which supports the answer's contrast with strict P4.

record_contradictions.record_says: notes/literature-check.md §3: "No statement independent of the group was found; Finkelstein 2008 (arXiv 2006) only speculates, in one sentence, that the momentum-energy coordinates of quantum events may contribute to dark matter (related, one agent's label)." The round-1 log has Sheng Ran's report as 'report not found', and workflow1-result.json as 'Sheng Ran not retrieved'.
record_contradictions.note: Quotations of source and record are verbatim (Ran's PDF; note lines 169–171; round1/g1-conjugate-matter.web_queries.json; workflow1-result.json). The source says what the reader says, and v1 says it too: the v1 PDF (dated 15 December 2025, posted 24 December 2025) differs from v2 only in its date line and reference formatting. But the record did not miss the report. Round 3 retrieved it (PDF and Wayback abstract), verified four quotes and labeled it C1 'partial'. Its verifier downgraded the label to 'related' (round3/oa-c1-c6-c7.verify.json; findings.json key doi:10.55277/researchhub.unu7fof1.1, basis 'verified'), because the report 'never says dark matter is the counterpart of ordinary matter' and because of the rule for non-reviewed venues. The round-3 sweep's statement, carried into panel/C1.evidence.json, even says that 'no source other than Sheng Ran's removed ResearchHub preprint states that dark matter is the matter of momentum space, the conjugate or reciprocal sector, the dual half of phase space'. What survives is narrower than the reader claims. By the record's own labels the note's sentence is defensible, since every anticipates is the school's. It is incomplete: it names Finkelstein's one-sentence speculation (related) as the outside near-miss and omits Ran's report (related, verified), which states its result as a finding. The record's 'removed' is also inexact. The landing pages 404, but both CC-BY PDFs still download from storage.prod.researchhub.com, and OpenAlex lists v2's PDF. That the report is C1's core is the reader's judgement, against the record's verified label; it rests on the §2 reading in which ordinary momentum at ℏ belongs to C1.

record_contradictions.record_says: wiki/method/literature-check.md, C1 'Not found': "the identification joined to a sector coupled to ours by gravity alone (mirror and twin matter couple by gravity, without reciprocity)"; flag 64: "Copies of ordinary matter coupled to ours mainly or only by gravity are published without reciprocity (mirror and twin matter); joined to the identification they were not found."; note §3: "All nine come from one group and carry one priority, Minic 2020".
record_contradictions.note: Source and record wording are quoted correctly (Crossref abstracts of Häuser–Dröscher Parts II and III; Nishimura full text; wiki row line 45; flag 64; note line 166). A grep of the repository outside work/ finds neither paper. As the reader says, this qualifies the record rather than contradicting it. The 'Not found' cell is about the identification joined to gravity-only coupling, and neither paper states the identification: their dual spacetimes are an imaginary-time dual de Sitter space and an internal isospin spacetime, not momentum space. Two corrections. (1) For Häuser–Dröscher, 'by gravity alone' is an inference from abstracts ('principally invisible', 'principally undetectable', gravitational interaction 'directly perceptible'); no 'only' is stated. (2) Nishimura goes further than reported. As a conditional, his negative-norm sector, assigned to the dual isospin spacetime, coupled by gravity alone and proposed as the dark side, would hold 'almost all the antiparticles'. That makes it a counterpart of visible matter in a dual space, though not a Born dual. The record's examples of published gravity-only copies could add these dual-spacetime cases. Part II (online 2019-04-10) predates Minic 2020 by 325 days (scripts/day_gaps.py).

overall: The reader's quotations are reliable: all 110 statement quotations and 49 answer fragments were found verbatim (lit.py, or PDFs I downloaded myself), and the arXiv v1 dates match the arXiv API. Most readings hold, but three things are overstated: the record already had Ran's report (C1 related, verified), so the first contradiction reduces to an incomplete sentence in note §3; the step from Ran to #11 §11.4's hiding conditions fails; and the universal claims in Q1, Q3 and Q7 are contradicted by Addazi et al., Huang and Huang, Pavšič and Ran's own wave state. The most consequential omission is Yargic's 2021 thesis speculation that breaking the modular U(1) could fix the configuration space, the nearest outside statement to #11's spontaneous selection of the polarization.
